thread:
anya: kicked off an FP8 kernel enablement canary across h100 and l40s for atlas-13b. small shadow traffic (2.5k requests) yesterday, full 10k run completed this morning. sharing early notes.

sanjay: nice — did you run both legacy fp8 path and the new tiled kernel? any perf diffs?

anya: ran two variants: fp8-legacy (current runtime) and fp8-tiled-kernel (new handshake). perf: tiled gives ~1.18x throughput on h100, ~1.09x on l40s. p50 latency mostly unchanged for short queries, p95 improved ~4-6% on h100.

igor: quality side — what eval suite? any regen on our hallucination prompt set?

anya: evals: 8k eval prompts (mix of summarization, instruction, longchain Q&A). overall lm perplexity delta +0.4% vs fp16 baseline for tiled kernel. but a tail of ~120 prompts showed regressions >1.5% (mostly long-prefix summarization).

marie: can you post an example of failure mode? rough snippet or token-level diff helps.

anya: pasted sample in thread (trimmed):
```
input: "Summarize meeting notes covering product strategy over 14,000 chars"
fp16: "...teams will prioritize Q3 integration..."
fp8-tiled: "...teams will focus on integration next quarter."
metric: rouge-l drop 2.1, factuality flag triggered on 1 of 3 checks
```
Most diffs are soft paraphrases but some factual attritions triggered our QA rules.

taylor: interesting — could be kv-cache tiling handshake losing prefix alignment for very long contexts. did you repro with kv-cache disabled?

anya: yes. disabling kv-cache removes ~80% of the large-delta cases, so kv handshake looks suspect. but disabling cache regresses performance so can't ship like that.

igor: did you try the hybrid fallback (fp8 for attention matmul, fp16 for prefix-heavy attention) or AWQ/GPTQ variants for comparison?

anya: ran quick AWQ and GPTQ on same model: AWQ-int8 had smaller quality deltas overall (+0.2% perplexity) but cost was worse on L40S due to kernel mismatch. GPTQ had larger variance; some tiny hallucination increases. The tiled fp8 path seems best perf-wise but kv handshake needs robustness fixes.

marie: any telemetry signals beyond rouge/perplexity? user-facing logs, top tokens diffs, confidence calibration shifts?

anya: yes — calibration drift for long prefixes: softmax peakiness decreased slightly (temp-like smoothing), which explains paraphrase tendency. token-level entropy +0.08 on average for regressed examples.

sanjay: ops question — were any runs hitting numeric saturation / infs / NaNs?

anya: only one transient NaN in fp8-legacy warmup on h100 early morning; mitigated by activation clipping patch (applied in canary v2). tiled kernel had no NaNs but showed micro-batching variance where different tile order produced small numeric offsets.

igor: propose plan: 1) add a kv-handshake unit test with long-prefix fuzz (coverage for tile boundaries), 2) run 100k shadow requests with KV disabled/enabled to quantify tradeoffs, 3) add automatic rollback rule: if regression >1% rouge-l on watchlist prompts, route to fp16 variant.

taylor: agree. also add metric to console: "kv-handshake-mismatch-rate" and trace tile indices in traces for failing requests.

deploy-bot: canary deployment 3304509876 -> fp8-tiled-kernel: status=deployed to canary pool size=12 gpus, started=3304509900

marie: I'll draft a short runbook for oncall: how to toggle fp8 kernel, patch to disable kv-cache, and steps to rollback to fp16. also include how to collect problematic requests for debugging.

anya: thanks. I'll push the kv-handshake test and upload the 120 failing prompts to the eval bucket (path: gs://redwood-evals/fp8/3304509876-watchlist). will follow up with a small PR for tiling trace flags.

sanjay: thumbs up. keep the watchlist tight — prioritize hallucination/factuality prompts + longprefix summarization. aim to have hard-stop gating in 24h if regressions persist. :thumbsup:
